question: Which price source will we originate and grade against, at what timestamp, and under what licence?
blocks: Every edge, every CLV number, every strategy promotion, and 9 of the 14 gates in the root register
have: Nothing. No odds feed is reachable from this environment and no price is committed to the repository
lack: Opening and closing spread, total, moneyline and prop prices; a captured-at timestamp per price; a licence to store and re-serve them
how_to_close: Pick one vendor tier (exchange, book or aggregator), then backfill two full seasons with timestamps before any strategy is called skill-based

question: What is the authoritative source for who actually started and who was inactive?
blocks: The entire "2nd/3rd/4th string is playing" requirement, replacement-cost estimates, and snap-based props
have: Official NFL game books, which list both starting lineups and full inactive lists for all 136 completed games, linked from every game page
lack: Nothing blocking: the books are reachable. What is missing is a parser and a stored copy
how_to_close: Adopt the game book as the availability ground truth, version the PDFs, and derive the lineup from them rather than from a depth chart the league does not publish

question: Is a depth rank (1st through 4th string) needed at all, given that the game book proves who started?
blocks: Any feature that claims to know a player's depth slot
have: Proof that the league publishes no depth chart (confirmed: the path returns the league 404 page); club sites publish charts for 12 to 13 clubs
lack: A league-wide depth rank; a rule for what "3rd string" means when the starter and his backup are both active
how_to_close: Replace depth rank with measured participation: start, share of snaps, and active or inactive. Rank becomes a derived label, not an input

question: What is the minimum sample that can distinguish skill from luck on a single-bet strategy?
blocks: The reward tiers on the leaderboard and any claim that a strategy is "selectively skill based"
have: Exact arithmetic: at a 52.4% break-even and 136 games observed, a 95% band on ROI is about 8.9 points at n=100 and 1.6 points at n=3,000
lack: Agreement on the false-positive budget, and a stake size that does not compound the error
how_to_close: Set the gate at n >= 1,000 settled bets with a pre-registered one-sided test, and publish the band rather than the point estimate

question: Do team scores within a game behave as independent, or is there a shared pace effect?
blocks: Parlay and same-game pricing, which currently assume independence
have: A measured answer on 136 games: home vs away points r = +0.076; total vs margin r = -0.016. The shared-pace story is weak
lack: A price archive to convert that into a parlay price error in dollars
how_to_close: Recompute on every new week and publish the interval. Do not assert a parlay markup until a price feed exists (XQ-01)

question: How many of the 25 players added to the injury page after our snapshot matter for a Week 10 number?
blocks: Any Week 10 pricing or availability claim
have: The exact diff: 25 rows added, 4 practice cells changed, all in IND, SEA, CIN, SF, JAX, AZ
lack: A check of whether each added player is a starter, which needs XQ-02
how_to_close: Join the live table to the game book inactive list at kickoff; publish the difference rather than overwrite the snapshot

question: Which of the 14 "correlations" across the repository are independent findings and which are the same calculation repeated?
blocks: Any claim about how much evidence exists
have: Four trees publish n=32 team correlations: 12, 14, 15 and 6 coefficients. C-01 in two trees is the identical pair at r = 0.876
lack: A provenance record stating which tree a number came from and whether an outside party can recompute it
how_to_close: Declare the root register the system of record; mark the other trees as parallel evidence with their own generators

question: What does the reward for a top strategy actually pay, and who funds it?
blocks: The competition half of the brief; "rewards for top performing strategies"
have: Tiers and rules written in the root register; no funding mechanism, no settlement ledger, no unit definition tied to money
lack: A funding source, a settlement currency, and a rule for what happens when a strategy is retired
how_to_close: Decide whether the reward is reputational (rank only) or monetary. If monetary, define the bankroll and the unit first

question: Is player-level data (snaps, routes, targets) available to us, or must everything be built from public box scores?
blocks: Prop modelling and any prop-combination correlation
have: Per-game official statistics from the game books: rushing, passing, receiving with targets, plus starters and inactives
lack: Snaps, routes run, coverage assignments and per-play participation
how_to_close: Estimate snap share from the substitution list only as a coarse proxy and label it as such, or license a provider

question: What is the acceptable data-staleness budget for a table a reader will act on?
blocks: Every page that presents a count as current
have: Two fetches four hours apart already differ: 254 rows became 279, and two clubs that read "No Injuries Reported" now publish rows
lack: A stated budget, and a build that refuses to render an unlabelled count without its fetch time
how_to_close: Publish the fetch instant on every measured number and fail the build if a count has no timestamp

question: Which team abbreviation standard binds the data?
blocks: Any join between the schedule, the standings and the club pages
have: The league itself is inconsistent: the schedule codes the Rams LA while the standings code them LAR, and the game page uses LAR
lack: A single crosswalk committed as data, not as a code alias
how_to_close: Commit an explicit alias table and make the build fail on an unmapped code

question: Does the 136-game log's rating model beat the closing line, or only beat a naive baseline?
blocks: Whether any originated line is worth publishing
have: A negative result in one tree (MAE 10.25 vs 9.94) that cannot be reproduced because no price archive is committed
lack: A committed price archive so the comparison is falsifiable
how_to_close: Adopt the comparison, not the number, until XQ-01 closes

question: What counts as "removing luck", concretely enough to gate a strategy?
have: Four independent filters already implemented in one tree: chronological split-half, season-to-season persistence, Wilson bounds, and a Bonferroni correction across 60 tests
lack: An agreed pass rule that combines them, and a holdout that has not already been looked at
how_to_close: Write the pass rule as one sentence per filter and freeze it before the next season starts

question: Who owns the decision to change a shared number when two trees disagree?
have: A documented rule that another session's file is an input, not a source
lack: A named owner and a single edit window per cycle
how_to_close: Keep the root register as the only writable system of record; other trees cite it
